chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch 488 — The Lord Tiger's Feast: Exorcism Gone Wrong
chapter_meta_description: Lian Zhibei performs a brutal tiger-possession ritual to cut Bai Lingmiao's Immortal link. But the cure destroys the Second Spirit. Li Huowang chooses wrong.
og_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch 488 — The Lord Tiger's Feast
og_description: A possessed medium's tiger ritual devours Bai Lingmiao's Immortal flesh — and the Second Spirit along with it. Li Huowang pays for his victory in blood and regret.
twitter_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch 488 — Tiger Spirit vs. Second Spirit
twitter_description: Lian Zhibei's exorcism works too well. The Second Spirit is erased. Li Huowang's arm goes flying. A messy, heartbreaking chapter.

lore_anchors.definition: A Chinese folk-religious practitioner who invites a deity into their body through self-mutilation; the body becomes pain-proof as proof of possession.
A wooden judge's block used in ritual theater or folk religion to command spirits and declare authority; Lian Zhibei slams it to seal the invocation.
A martial guardian spirit in Chinese folk religion, often invoked in exorcism to devour evil or possessing entities. The tiger is a symbol of raw, untamed yang power.

In a chuma possession ritual, the silent assistant medium who acts as a vessel for the spirit's companion. Here, she is revealed to be a fragment of Bai Lingmiao's own consciousness fused with the Immortals.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did Lian Zhibei’s ritual hurt the Second Spirit?
cultural_notes_faq.a: In the chuma / jitong system, the Second Spirit is not a separate ghost but a fragment of Bai Lingmiao’s own consciousness that grew around the Immortals’ flesh. When Lian Zhibei devours that flesh, she destroys the Second Spirit along with it.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did Li Huowang fight Lian Zhibei instead of just talking?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Lian Zhibei had lost awareness during the possession — she was running on pure tiger spirit instinct. Li Huowang’s shouts failed, so he had to physically stop her. By the time the incense burned out, both were already wounded.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is the Possessed Medium (起乩) a real practice?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Yes. In Chinese folk religion, *jitong* (possessed mediums) still exist. Self-mutilation with spikes and hooks is a traditional method to prove a god is truly inside the body, as the possessed should feel no pain.
